description: Rick's third Cornwall journey digs further into the county's rock pools, orchards, tea gardens, mining communities, artists, writers and working boats, repeatedly returning to the question of how a place preserves identity while still changing.

s13e01.description: Rick forages mussels from favourite rock pools and turns them into a seafood omelette, then explores the Charlotte Dymond murder story on Bodmin Moor and cooks soufflés with artisanal Cornish goat's cheese.

s13e02.description: Raynor Winn and Moth join Rick at a heritage cider orchard before he cooks chicken, leek and cider gratin, and a women's sea-shanty group shows how maritime music continues to change with the county.

s13e03.description: At Tregothnan, Rick visits Britain's unusual tea plantation and builds an afternoon tea, then heads to Penzance's Jubilee Pool and traces Cornwall's connection to Dickens and A Christmas Carol.

s13e04.description: The ancient settlement of Carn Euny opens a discussion of deep Cornish history before Rick visits Truro cattle market, cooks steak-and-kidney pudding and sees a replica of a historic Falmouth working boat.

s13e05.description: Rick sails with one of the crews still harvesting oysters under sail, cooks the catch into a Cullen-skink-style soup and follows paintings of local oystermen before exploring Lostwithiel, Cornwall's former capital.

s13e06.description: A red-deer farm supplies the venison for Rick's Wellington, while artist Hannah Woodman captures Porthgwarra's coast and comedian Jonny Cowling examines the stubbornly local character of Cornish humour.

s13e07.description: After crossing the River Fal on the King Harry Ferry, Rick visits an organic market garden and makes a radicchio tart, then explores composer Malcolm Arnold's Cornish connection with broadcaster Petroc Trelawny.

s13e08.description: Rick looks at the women who worked as bal maidens in Cornwall's mining industry, visits a church preserving centuries-old wall paintings and follows local botanicals into an elaborately named platinum pudding.

s13e09.description: Rick demonstrates steamed sea bass with ginger and garlic, visits a potter in the far west and travels to Launceston to explore poet Charles Causley with novelist Patrick Gale.

s13e10.description: A Boscastle seafood restaurant housed in a former rocket station leads to an organic mushroom farm and a lion's-mane stir-fry, before the series closes in Mousehole with the surprising German afterlife of Rosamunde Pilcher's Cornwall.
